clue.text: Book here!

definitions.meaning: a book, especially a weighty volume
a call to bring something over, as in 'pass it this way, to my side!'

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits into two words: 'here!' is what you say meaning 'give it TO ME'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy book; 'here!' as a summons means pass it over to the speaker.

clue.text: Pinch awake in Turkey

indicators.note: the waking word goes inside the Turkey letters

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
to rouse is to awake or wake up

explanation.surface: Someone is pinched awake while in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: To trouser is British slang for pocketing money, often dishonestly, hence 'pinch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser as a verb is informal for put in one's pocket, so to take or steal.

clue.text: E.g. newspapers with immoral article instead of one that's primitive

parts.note: newspapers are an example of the media

indicators.note: the article letter goes where the one letter was

parts.note: evil means wicked or immoral
I is the Roman numeral for one
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Newspapers with a smutty article are accused of being backward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead of' replaces the I of EVIL with A, giving EVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediaeval, relating to the Middle Ages, is used loosely to mean crude or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Get shock when gold mark's given for third part of essay

indicators.note: says something is put in place of the third letter of the essay word

parts.note: a treatise is a long written essay on a subject
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
M is a standard abbreviation for mark, as in the old German currency

explanation.surface: A student is shocked when a gold star is awarded for one section of an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given for third part of' swaps the third letter, E, of TREATISE for AU and M.
explanation.definitionFit: To traumatise someone is to give them a severe emotional shock.

clue.text: Foul and/or noxious gas

indicators.note: foul means fouled up or mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a gas may be foul, or noxious, or both.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' rearranges the letters of AND and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive gas, harmful to breathe in, an element that seeps from rocks.

clue.text: In EastEnders, search for staff's private room where no one has been

indicators.note: EastEnders is the BBC soap set in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the h

parts.note: to hunt is to search for
a rod is a staff or stick
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A soap character hunts for a staff room that nobody has entered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In EastEnders' drops the H of HUNT, Cockney style, giving UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrodden ground has never been walked on, so it is unexplored territory.

clue.text: Rapidly bombard enemy sailor at navy's second uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising means the letters read upwards, so the whole run is written backwards

parts.note: to stonk is to bombard with heavy shellfire
a foe is an enemy
a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: the second letter of the navy word

explanation.surface: Forces bombard an enemy sailor during a naval mutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reverses the whole string STONKFOETARATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at a rate of knots is moving very fast, as a speeding ship does.

clue.text: Mesopotamian fragments of interred remains are quite interesting

indicators.note: fragments of the words means their opening letters

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds that pieces of buried remains are quite intriguing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Mesopotamia lay largely in what is now Iraq, so a Mesopotamian is a native of that land.

clue.text: Duck with no head protects bird with no end

indicators.note: the beheaded duck wraps around the bird
the duck word loses its first letter

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A headless duck shields a bird missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end' looks like another cut, matching 'with no head', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, without any end.

clue.text: Sorry — how rude of me, mistaking dancer for nymph

indicators.note: mistaking means getting it wrong, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for confusing a dancer with a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaking' rearranges DANCER FOR NYMPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular apology for swearing or rudeness, which pretends the foul word was a foreign one.

clue.text: She knows the ropes hold rocks, moreover

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters of hold are jumbled

parts.note: and means moreover, in addition

explanation.surface: A sailor woman who holds the rigging knows what she is doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' rearranges HOLD into OLDH.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is an experienced person, someone who is thoroughly familiar with how things are done.

clue.text: The fat crackles oddly in a bun

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the words: first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A cook watches fat sizzle in a pan while frying a bun.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'The fat' give TEA, and those of 'crackles' give CAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light, sweet bun, often with dried fruit, usually toasted and buttered.

clue.text: Warm praise for dog beset by hunger, carrying note for king

indicators.note: the dog is surrounded by the hunger word, so it goes inside
says the hunger word takes on a new letter in place of another
for marks the note letter standing in place of the king letter

parts.note: starvation is extreme hunger
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
a dingo is an Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: A starving hound earns lavish praise, as if a musical note were taking a king's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying ... for' makes the swap first, giving STANVATION; only then does 'beset by' wrap it round the dog. 'Warm' means hearty here, not hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing ovation is enthusiastic applause from an audience rising to its feet, the warmest kind of praise.

clue.text: Frantic call about a very upset mother

indicators.note: the call word goes around the next letters

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone

indicators.note: upset in a down clue sense of overturned, so the word for mother is turned back to front

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: Someone makes a frantic phone call to a mother who is very distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses DAM to MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Raving mad means completely crazy or frenzied, so wildly frantic.

clue.text: Silly me, soaking up European sun and humidity!

indicators.note: the silly word absorbs the next letter inside it

parts.note: muggins is a jokey name for oneself as a fool
S is short for sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker laughs at themselves for soaking up the sun in a humid European spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugginess is warm, damp, close weather, so a state of humidity.

clue.text: Best big clothing label, according to report

indicators.note: report means what is heard, so the letters are taken by their sound when spoken

parts.note: XL is the size label meaning extra large on clothes

explanation.surface: A shopper ranks the finest oversized clothing brand on the word of a report.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to outdo or surpass them, which is what to excel means.

clue.text: Burning money in production

indicators.note: the money letter goes into the production word

parts.note: a creation is something produced
M is short for money, as in M1 and M3 measures of money supply

explanation.surface: Money is being burnt on a film or stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremation is the burning of a corpse to ashes.

clue.text: Shout about following a passage

indicators.note: the turned shout comes after the letter a
about means turned around, so the shout word is written backwards

parts.note: to yell is to shout

explanation.surface: Someone shouts after reading a passage aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the shout round to LLEY; 'following' puts that after the A. 'passage' is a lane, not a piece of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow passage between buildings.

clue.text: Like a duck it rises, cutting a duck's cry short

indicators.note: the risen word cuts into the duck's cry
cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a duck's call is a quack

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: A duck takes off, its quack cut off mid-call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns the word upward to TI, and 'cutting' puts that inside A QUAC, the cry cut 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatic means living in or on water, as a duck does.

clue.text: Clung tight with feet to show respect

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and drunk letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clings on hard with their feet, perhaps while climbing, to show respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' rearranges CLUNG and FEET together.
explanation.definitionFit: To genuflect is to bend the knee in worship or deference, a gesture of respect.

clue.text: Flirt with posh, flighty models? You might find some here

definitions.text: models? You might find some here

parts.note: to toy with someone is to flirt or trifle with them

indicators.note: flighty means fickle and unsettled, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with posh, fickle fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' rearranges POSH into SHOP. 'models' means scale-model toys, not fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy shop sells miniature cars, trains and dolls, the kind of models a child collects.

clue.text: A prurient layman's naughty but a minister shouldn't be

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: what a government minister ought not to be in the House

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so these letters are disorderly and rearranged

explanation.surface: An ordinary man with a dirty mind may be naughty, but a politician must not be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges A PRURIENT LAYMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unparliamentary language breaks the rules of decorum in parliament, which a government member should avoid.

clue.text: Philosopher shown up by total pillock

indicators.note: shown up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A philosopher is exposed as a complete idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: A pillock is British slang for a fool. In a down clue 'shown up' reads the hidden run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato is the ancient Greek thinker who wrote the Republic, an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: E.g. Alaskan animal's low bearing

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
SE, south-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A wild Alaskan beast gives a low bellow as it holds its course.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose, the largest deer, roams Alaska, so it is one example of an animal found there.

clue.text: Apprentice's mouth never closes in content-free episode

indicators.note: the mouth word is never closed, so its final letter goes

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

indicators.note: with its contents gone, only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A trainee who talks nonstop fills an otherwise empty episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never closes' cuts the P from TRAP; 'content-free' empties EPISODE to EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a trade, just as an apprentice is.

clue.text: Wealthiest losing millions — one refuses to face facts

indicators.note: losing says the letter for millions is dropped

parts.note: most rich is a way of saying wealthiest
M is the abbreviation for million or millions

explanation.surface: The very rich, minus their millions, cannot bear to accept reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes the M from MOST RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostrich, from the bird said to bury its head in the sand, is someone who ignores unpleasant truths.

clue.text: Comic actor forgets washerwoman's tips, such as 'I hold laundry!'

indicators.note: forgets says letters are dropped from the comic word

parts.note: a clown is a comic performer

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: thesp is short for thespian, an actor
EG, for example, means such as

explanation.surface: A comedy actor forgets a washerwoman's advice about hanging laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgets' removes the washerwoman's tips W and N from CLOWN, leaving CLO; the speaker of 'I hold laundry!' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes peg clips wet washing to a line, so it is something that would say it holds laundry.

clue.text: I've got the same picture

definitions.meaning: the shout in a card game when two matching cards appear
a photograph, especially a quick one

explanation.definitionFit: Snap is the call in the children's card game on matching cards, and a snap is an informal photo.
